entities.name: Vienna Circle & Logical Positivism
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: A group of philosophers, mathematicians, and scientists meeting in Vienna (1924-1936) who developed logical positivism — the view that only empirically verifiable statements are meaningful. Led by Moritz Schlick and including Rudolf Carnap and Kurt Gödel, the Vienna Circle's emphasis on scientific verification, logical analysis, and the unity of science profoundly shaped 20th-century philosophy.
